title: Level 4 (Expert) - D-17
notes:
West leads the ♠7 against 3NT. There are 8 top tricks (3 spades, given the lead, 3 diamonds, and 2 clubs). The contract will be easy if diamonds are 3-2. South should therefore assume that diamonds are 4-1 and plan the play accordingly.

South should start by winning West's spade opening lead in hand (if South wins it in the dummy he may never get a third spade trick). The resulting blockage in spades creates a communications problem. South must play carefully to resolve this blockage due to the unfavorable lie of the East-West hearts and diamonds.

There is a safety play available that will virtually guarantee the contract. South should duck a diamond in both hands at trick 2 (it is fine to unblock the ♠A first). East will switch to the ♥Q which South must duck. East continues with the ♥J and this time South must cover with the ♥K. West wins the ♥A, but cannot effectively continue hearts from his side of the table.

South can win whatever West returns, unblock the ♠A if necessary, and cross to the closed hand in diamonds. South unblocks his remaining high diamond, cashes the ♠K, and then crosses to the dummy in clubs. South can now cash dummy's remaining diamonds to make his contract.
